title: Ovarian Torsion: Emergency Recognition, Ultrasound and Surgical Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Ovarian Torsion: Emergency Recognition, Ultrasound and Surgical Referral
findings: Built as an additive Disease Management version using the approved-topic structure.
Investigations are ordered from bedside/laboratory assessment to imaging and specialist tests.
The original outline remains current; this version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: The opened ACOG guidance is adolescent-focused; adult local gynaecology policy must also be applied.
Saudi operative and analgesic formulary details were not opened.

pathophysiology.summary: Twisting of the adnexal vascular pedicle impairs venous and lymphatic drainage. Progressive oedema can compromise arterial inflow and threaten ovarian viability. Intermittent torsion can produce episodic pain and normal flow between episodes.
keyMechanisms: Twisting of the adnexal vascular pedicle impairs venous and lymphatic drainage.
Progressive oedema can compromise arterial inflow and threaten ovarian viability.
Intermittent torsion can produce episodic pain and normal flow between episodes.

symptoms: Sudden unilateral lower abdominal/pelvic pain, often with nausea and vomiting.
physicalSigns: Lower abdominal tenderness; peritonism may indicate advanced ischaemia or another surgical emergency.
redFlags: Pregnancy, haemodynamic instability, peritonism, persistent severe pain or high clinical suspicion despite non-diagnostic imaging.
precipitants: Ovarian mass/cyst, enlarged ovary, pregnancy or fertility treatment; torsion can occur without a mass.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Positive pregnancy test with pregnancy-location pathway findings.
Typical migration/systemic inflammatory pattern; overlap is common.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Immediately activates pregnancy-location and ectopic-risk assessment without excluding torsion.

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise and refer
actions: Give analgesia, keep nil by mouth, obtain IV access and contact gynaecology urgently.
Treat pregnancy and haemodynamic instability through the appropriate emergency pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Image without delaying surgery
actions: Arrange pelvic ultrasound with Doppler while maintaining clinical suspicion.
Do not use normal Doppler flow as a rule-out test.

clinicalManagement.title: Operate when suspected
actions: Perform diagnostic laparoscopy with detorsion and ovarian preservation where feasible.
Further cyst/mass management follows age, operative findings and specialist judgement.

medicationPlan.note: No medicine detorses the adnexa. Give local age/pregnancy-appropriate analgesia and antiemetic therapy while arranging urgent surgery; exact agents and doses follow the emergency and anaesthetic formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Surgical visualisation; no clinical or Doppler criterion safely excludes torsion.

teaching.scope: Ovarian Torsion: Emergency Recognition, Ultrasound and Surgical Referral
learningObjectives: Recognise the emergency and relevant red flags.
Select the correct investigation and escalation pathway.
Use medicines only within the stated branch and local formulary.
pitfalls: Delaying specialist escalation while waiting for a non-essential test.
Using an unverified medicine dose or applying an adult pathway to a child.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval.
keyPoints: Pregnancy, haemodynamic instability, peritonism, persistent severe pain or high clinical suspicion despite non-diagnostic imaging.

patientEducation: Explain that imaging cannot fully exclude torsion and surgery may be needed to save the ovary.
lifestyleAndDiet: No specific lifestyle intervention during the emergency episode.
mdtReferrals: Urgent gynaecology; paediatric/adolescent gynaecology when applicable.
dischargeCriteria: Only after specialist exclusion or postoperative stability with safety-net advice.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Gynaecology follow-up for pathology, ovarian function and recurrence risk.
